extracted.intended_audience: small law firms and SMMEs in South Africa
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for small law firms and small/medium micro enterprises (SMMEs) in South Africa on planning, budgeting, resourcing, and maintaining intellectual property (trade marks, patents, designs, copyright) and using official IP resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capture IP deadlines and schedule regular reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadlines and due dates can be captured for action as an element of your business plan. An internal audit should also be conducted annually to ensure your IP strategy is still aligned with the business strategy. Quarterly objectives and requirements can be recorded for follow up and timeous action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record all filing, renewal, prosecution and enforcement deadlines in the business plan; schedule an annual internal audit to verify alignment between IP strategy and business goals; set and record quarterly objectives/requirements for follow-up and timely action so that tasks are tracked and completed on time.

rubrics_metrics.name: IP budgeting: include all protection and maintenance costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the costs of securing protection (filing, examination, prosecution, registration, renewals), and maintenance of IPRs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing an IP budget, include filing, examination, prosecution, registration, renewals and ongoing maintenance costs for each IPR. Request projected costs from external IP partners annually to support budgeting and to anticipate foreseeable costs for the financial year. Use the budgeting exercise to inform annual goals and enforcement objectives so enforcement-related costs can also be estimated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for unforeseeable costs and include a budget buffer
rubrics_metrics.description: Change in circumstances and unforeseeable costs, such as infringements of the IPRs or foreign exchange rate fluctuations, should be catered for in the budget to ensure you have the means to take the necessary action to protect your IP in your business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is recommended to include a buffer (10-20%) to cater for variances between budgeted and actual costs. Assess IP costs quarterly together with your business budget review to see whether any adjustments need to be made to meet the objectives and goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage external IP partners for annual cost forecasting and support
rubrics_metrics.description: This can be requested from the external IP partner annually to support and assist with budgeting of foreseeable costs for the financial year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask your external IP attorney/agent or IP service provider to prepare an annual forecast of expected filing, prosecution, registration, renewal and enforcement costs. Use their input to populate budgets and to identify potential risk areas (e.g., foreign filings, likely oppositions or enforcement actions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use official CIPC and sector resources and guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: PART 5 RESOURCES: Glossary of terms and abbreviations; CIPC additional resources and information; IP Directory and Information; Main IP Laws, Regulations and Treaties. Links and descriptions to CIPC pages (Register Trade Marks checklist, Life Cycle of trade marks, Nice Classification, Trade Mark Examination Guidelines, IPOnline, forms & fees) and numerous other national and international IP organisations are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the CIPC materials (checklist for trade mark registration, lifecycle of a trade mark, Nice classification lists, Trade Mark Examination Guidelines Version 3A, IPOnline e-filing guides, forms & fees) and relevant bodies (WIPO AMC, ARIPO, OAPI, DFFE guidance on ABS, WIPO resources on valuation, domain dispute providers, funding agencies like TIA/SEDA/SPII/THRIP) for procedural requirements, classifications, dispute resolution, and funding opportunities. Use these official resources as authoritative references when preparing filings, compliance checks, audits and budgets.
